1.explanation:
• ToggleElementCollapseBehaviour.js is where the ‘collapse’ action is implemented; it re‐computes the collapsed container’s bounds based on its children. Turning on the Ad Hoc marker fires this same code path unintentionally, shrinking the shape.  
• BpmnLayouter.js contains the layout logic used during collapse/expand and replace, and is responsible for determining default and minimum sizes. A bug here would lead to unexpected dimension changes when the element type changes.  
• BpmnUpdater.js updates the underlying BPMN DI (diagram interchange) information—i.e. the shape bounds—and is invoked on both collapse and replace, so any shrink is written back to the diagram.  
• BpmnReplace.js (the replace feature) drives the switch to the Ad Hoc Sub Process type; it kicks off a sequence that ends up re‐collapsing/re‐laying out the shape.  
• ReplaceElementBehaviour.js hooks into the modeling command stack for element replacement. It chains together type substitution and layout calls (including the collapse logic).  

Together these files are responsible for toggling collapse and replacing the subprocess type (to Ad Hoc) and then re‐computing/saving its bounds—exactly where the unwanted size change is happening.
1.bug_scenario: In the supplied GIF you start with an expanded Sub Process (with a child element inside), collapse it (works as expected) and then turn it into an Ad Hoc Sub Process. As soon as you switch to the Ad Hoc variant, the collapsed subprocess container is re‐sized (it snaps to the bounding box of its child), even though the user didn’t explicitly resize it. In other words, turning the already‐collapsed subprocess into an Ad Hoc subprocess triggers a recomputation of its width and height, making the red dashed outline shrink around the circle event, instead of preserving the original collapsed dimensions.

2.explanation:
- ToggleElementCollapseBehaviour.js: This behavior is responsible for collapsing/expanding subprocesses and kicking off layout updates; it governs how bounds are reset when the subprocess state changes.  
- ResizeUtil.js: Contains utilities that enforce minimum dimensions when shapes are resized or state-toggled; its thresholds are currently applied on collapse/ad-hoc toggle and lead to unwanted size changes.  
- BpmnLayouter.js: Computes the dimensions of subprocesses based on contents or markers (including the Ad-Hoc circle). When toggling the Ad-Hoc marker it recomputes bounds and currently ignores the last collapsed size.  
- BpmnUpdater.js: Persists the updated bounds (DI) after modeling commands run; this commits the incorrect size back into the diagram.  
- BpmnAutoResizeProvider.js: Listens for shape changes (including collapse/expand and marker toggles) and triggers auto-resize operations which apply ResizeUtil’s minimum sizes, contributing to the jump in dimensions when you turn on the Ad-Hoc marker.
2.bug_scenario: When you collapse an expanded subprocess containing children, then convert that collapsed subprocess into an Ad-Hoc subprocess, its outer boundary box snaps back to the wrong dimensions (you can see the dashed resize indicator change size unexpectedly). In the provided GIF you create a subprocess with a child inside, collapse it (making it small), then toggle on the Ad-Hoc marker and the subprocess jumps to an incorrect size instead of preserving its current collapsed dimensions.
